newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to privatise 30 fuel stations.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to privatise 30 fuel stations.

text.p: Kuwait's Supreme Petroleum Council has approved the privatisation of 30 roadside petrol stations, al-Watan newspaper reported on Sunday.
The council approved "the privatisation of 30 fuel stations as a first trial to privatise other stations," the daily said.
The council met on Saturday under the oil-rich state's foreign minister, Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah, also a deputy prime minister.

The state's Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) said last year it was preparing a timetable for privatising some operations including domestic fuel stations which in Kuwait are all owned by the government.
Since 1994 Kuwait has sold its stake in some 18 local firms for over $2 billion in the first phase of a privatisation plan while 36 more worth some $3 billion still remain, officials say.
Kuwait hopes to gain parliamentary approval in 1997 to start the next and more controversial stages of privatising public utilities like water, electricity and health care.
